transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Hello, doctor. When I try to talk things through with people, my thoughts get all jumbled and I can’t seem to keep a straight line in a conversation anymore. It's just very frustrating because I want to express myself, but everything gets so mixed up.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'jumbled thoughts' - do you experience any voices or sounds that aren't there, or do your thoughts just feel disjointed and hard to put into words?

No, I don't hear any voices or sounds, it's just that my thoughts feel so disjointed and hard to put into words. I'll start trying to say something simple, like about the electric bill, but then I get completely off track talking about my husband's toolbox, choir songs, or the weather all mixed together. It just leaves everyone, including myself, feeling so confused.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless most of the time, or has your mood been more stable despite the difficulties with your thoughts?

Of course I miss my husband dearly, but I'm not really sure if I would say I feel empty or hopeless most of the time. It's just that my mind gets so terribly mixed up, and my main struggle is really how jumbled my thoughts get when I try to talk to people.
When did you first notice that your thoughts were getting jumbled and hard to express, was it a sudden change or something that came on gradually over time?

It didn't happen overnight, doctor; it has been creeping in gradually over the past year. It really started some time after my husband passed away, and it has just slowly gotten worse as the months have gone by.
Can you describe if there are any specific triggers or situations that make your thoughts feel more jumbled, or if it happens consistently across different conversations and topics?

It happens pretty consistently during normal, everyday conversations with my daughter or my friends at church, without any real trigger. I'll just try to talk about something simple, like the electric bill, and suddenly my mind drifts off to choir songs, my husband's toolbox, or the weather. It just seems to happen no matter what we are trying to discuss.
Have you noticed any difficulties with your memory, such as forgetting recent events, appointments, or tasks you need to complete?

Yes, I've had a lot of trouble keeping my tasks straight and have missed several appointments and choir rehearsals. My daughter now has to come over every week to manage my mail and bills to make sure I don't miss payments or important dates. At first, my family and friends thought it was just normal aging or grief after my husband passed.

Have you experienced any significant changes in your ability to perform daily activities, such as cooking, cleaning, or managing your finances, aside from the difficulties with conversations and memory?

Yes, it's been quite embarrassing, but I've really struggled to manage things on my own. I used to love organizing our church dinners, but now they gently leave me off the planning lists because I get too confused. My daughter has had to completely take over sorting my mail and bills to make sure everything gets paid on time.
Can you tell me if you've noticed any decline in your ability to learn new things or adapt to new situations, and if so, how that compares to your difficulties with jumbled thoughts and memory?

I'm not quite sure about learning new things, because I haven't really tried to learn anything new lately. I've just been having such a hard time managing my usual, familiar routine and keeping my thoughts straight during normal conversations.
Have you experienced any problems with disorientation, such as getting lost in familiar places or having trouble understanding the time of day or the day of the week?

No, I haven't really experienced getting lost in places I know well, or losing track of the day or time. It's more just that my mind gets so jumbled and disorganized when I'm trying to talk to people or do my normal activities.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to make decisions or solve problems, and if so, can you give me an example of how this has affected your daily life?

Yes, making decisions and keeping track of things has become very hard for me because I get so easily confused. I used to organize our church dinners and handle my own bills, but now my daughter has to sort my mail, pay the bills, and manage my appointments so I don't miss anything.

Can you tell me if you've noticed any significant changes in your physical abilities, such as difficulty with walking, balance, or coordination, in addition to the cognitive and conversational challenges you're experiencing?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with my walking, balance, or physical coordination. My physical mobility seems to be generally fine. It is really just my thoughts and getting mixed up that I struggle with.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your emotional state or behavior, such as apathy, agitation, or mood swings, in addition to the cognitive symptoms you've described?

No, I haven't really noticed feeling particularly apathetic, agitated, or having major mood swings. My mood has been pretty stable, and it's really just my thoughts and getting mixed up that I struggle with.
Have you noticed any changes in your use of alcohol or substances since your husband passed away, or have you been using them more frequently as a way to cope with your grief or jumbled thoughts?
No, doctor, I don't drink alcohol or use any substances to cope with things. That is not something I have ever done, so there hasn't been any change like that at all.

Can you think of any significant life events or health changes, aside from your husband's passing, that might have contributed to the gradual decline in your cognitive abilities and communication skills over the past year?

No, doctor, I really can't think of any other major life events or health changes besides losing my husband and trying to live on my own. I'm just not sure what else could have caused my thoughts to get so mixed up like this.

Have you experienced any difficulties with language, such as finding the right words, understanding written or spoken language, or following instructions, in addition to the jumbled thoughts you've described?

I don't really have trouble finding single words, but I struggle a lot with following conversations, especially when we are trying to plan things. My thoughts get so jumbled that I lose my train of thought, which makes it very hard to follow instructions or keep my tasks straight like I used to at church.

Can you describe if you have experienced any decline in your ability to perform tasks that require planning, sequencing, or organization, and if so, how that has impacted your daily life and interactions with others?

Yes, I've had a very hard time with planning and keeping things organized lately. I used to help organize our church dinners and manage my own bills, but now people at church gently leave me off the planning lists because I get too jumbled up. My daughter has to come over every week now to handle my mail, payments, and appointments so I don't get completely overwhelmed.

Can you tell me if you've noticed a significant decline in your cognitive abilities, such as memory, language, or problem-solving, that has been progressively worsening over the past year, and if so, how that has affected your daily life and ability to function independently?

Yes, doctor, these problems with getting mixed up and losing my train of thought have definitely been getting worse over this past year. It has made it very hard to function on my own, especially since I can no longer manage my bills or organize church events like I used to. My daughter actually has to come over every single week now just to sort through my mail and handle my payments.

You mentioned that your symptoms started after your husband passed away and have been gradually worsening over the past year. Can you clarify if there was a noticeable acceleration or significant change in your cognitive decline at any point during this year, or has it been a relatively steady progression?

It has been a mostly gradual progression, creeping in steadily over the past year since my husband passed. However, for at least the last six months, those confusing spells where my thoughts and actions feel completely out of step with everyone around me have become a regular, very noticeable part of my life.

You've mentioned a gradual progression of your symptoms over the past year, but can you tell me if there was any specific point or period where you felt your cognitive decline accelerated or worsened more significantly than at other times?

While the mix-ups have been gradually creeping in for about a year since my husband passed, the past six months have felt much more intense. That is when these really confusing spells, where my thoughts and actions feel completely out of step with everyone else, started happening on a regular basis.

Can you clarify if the worsening of your symptoms over the past six months has been associated with any changes in your daily functioning, such as increased dependence on your daughter for daily tasks or further decline in your ability to manage your own affairs?

Yes, there has been a very big change in how I manage on my own. I used to handle all my bills and help organize church dinners, but now the church ladies gently leave me off the planning lists. My daughter has had to start coming over every single week to sort my mail, pay the bills, and keep track of my appointments.

You've described a gradual decline in your cognitive abilities over the past year, with a noticeable increase in severity over the last six months. Can you tell me if you've experienced any episodes of sudden, significant worsening of your symptoms, or has the progression been relatively steady with minor fluctuations?

No, doctor, I haven't had any sudden, sharp spikes in my symptoms. It has been a very steady and gradual progression, slowly creeping in since the year after my husband passed. It has just become more regular and noticeable over the last six months rather than coming on all at once.
Have you experienced any episodes where your cognitive symptoms, such as jumbled thoughts or memory issues, seemed to improve significantly for a short period, only to worsen again?

No, doctor, I haven't really noticed any times where my thoughts became significantly clearer or improved. Instead, the confusion and jumbled thoughts have just been steadily creeping in and happening on a regular basis.

Can you compare the rate of decline in your cognitive abilities, such as memory and conversation skills, to your physical abilities, and tell me if one seems to be worsening more quickly than the other?

I haven't really noticed any decline in my physical abilities, so I'm not quite sure how to compare them. It is really my thinking and my jumbled conversations that are causing me the most trouble and making things so difficult.
Can you tell me if you've experienced any difficulties with recognizing familiar people, places, or objects, which might help differentiate between the possible causes of your cognitive symptoms?

No, doctor, I haven't had any trouble recognizing my family, friends, or familiar places. I know exactly who everyone is and where I am; it's just my thoughts that get all jumbled up when I try to talk to them.
Can you tell me if you've experienced any significant changes in your judgment or ability to make sound decisions, and if so, how that has impacted your daily life and interactions with others?

Yes, I have had a lot of trouble managing things that require good judgment and decision-making, like keeping up with my bills, home repairs, and organizing events. Because of this, my friends at church have gently stopped including me on planning committees, and my daughter now has to come over every week to handle my mail and payments.

You've mentioned a gradual decline in your cognitive abilities over the past year, but can you tell me if you think the progression of your symptoms is more closely related to your age and the natural aging process, or if it seems more connected to the grief and stress you've experienced since your husband passed away?
I'm not really sure which one it is, doctor. I just know that things have been very difficult and confusing for me since my husband passed away, and it's hard to tell what is causing it.

Do you think your difficulties with jumbled thoughts and memory issues are more related to the emotional pain of losing your husband or to a noticeable decline in your mental sharpness and ability to focus?

At first, my family and I thought the confusion was just from the grief of losing my husband and adjusting to living alone. But because it has been going on for nearly a year and has gotten so much worse, it now feels like a real decline in my mental sharpness rather than just emotional pain. My thoughts are just completely jumbled now, and I can't seem to keep a conversation straight anymore.

Can you describe any situations or activities where you feel your cognitive abilities, such as memory or conversation skills, are relatively preserved or less affected, which might help us understand the nature of your decline?

To be honest, doctor, I can't really think of any activities or situations where my thinking feels clear or unaffected anymore. This confusion and jumbled feeling seem to impact almost everything I try to do these days. It is just very hard to find any area where I feel like my old self is preserved.

You've mentioned a gradual decline in your cognitive abilities over the past year, but can you tell me if you've noticed any difference in the rate of decline between different cognitive functions, such as memory, language, or problem-solving, that might help us narrow down the possible causes?

I'm not really sure, doctor, and I haven't really thought about it in that way before. It just feels like everything—my talking, my memory, and keeping tasks straight—has generally become much more jumbled and hard to keep track of lately.
Can you compare the progression of your cognitive decline to any physical health changes you've experienced since your husband passed away, such as changes in appetite, sleep, or energy levels?

I haven't really noticed or thought about any specific changes in my physical health, appetite, sleep, or energy levels since my husband passed. My body feels about the same as it always has. It is really just my mind and these jumbled thoughts that are causing me all this trouble.
